Guides

Website for a hair salon or beauty salon

A new client compares two or three salons before choosing. She looks at prices, photos and how easy it is to book. The salon that shows all this clearly is one step ahead.

Prices first

It is the first thing people look for, and the first thing many salons hide. A clear price list avoids calls “just for a price” and reassures: nobody likes discovering the amount at the till.

Write your services the way you say them in the salon: women's cut, colour, balayage, facial, waxing. These are exactly the words your clients type into Google.

Your work in photos

In your trade, the result shows. A few photos of your cuts, your colours or your treatment room are far more appealing than a long introduction.

Always ask the person's permission before publishing their photo. A simple “can I put it on my website?” is enough, and most people happily say yes.

Booking appointments

Your website should make booking easy, whatever way you work:

  • You take bookings by phone: a big call button, visible as soon as the page opens.
  • You use an online booking calendar: a “Book an appointment” button leads straight to your calendar.
  • You prefer to be contacted in writing: a short form that lands in your inbox.
  • You do not have a booking calendar yet: the Appointment booking option, at €100 once, lets your clients pick a time slot directly on the website.

What brings in new clients

A client who has just moved in types “hairdresser” followed by the name of her area or town. To show up, two things matter: your Google listing with real reviews, and a website that says clearly where you are and what you do.

With the Ongoing SEO extra, at €10 a month, I work on your SEO to move the salon up in these searches.

Which website for a salon?

The one-page website is the right choice for the vast majority of salons. It includes the introduction, prices, photos, opening hours and contact, delivered in 3 to 5 days.

If you have several areas (hair, beauty, nails, product sales), the showcase website gives each one its own page. Both cost €500.

Opening hours and holidays

A salon often changes its hours: late opening, exceptional closure, holidays. You tell me in your client area, and the site is up to date without you having to learn anything.

Your questions

Should I show all my prices on the website?

I recommend it. Services whose price depends on length or work can be shown with “from”. What matters is that the client has a rough idea before coming.

I work alone from home, is a website useful?

Yes, maybe even more so: with no shop front on the street, your website and your Google listing are the only places people can find you. A one-page website is more than enough.

Can I link my online booking calendar?

Yes. If you already use a booking service, the button on the site leads straight to it. If not, a call button and a form do the job very well. And if you want people to book online, there is the Appointment booking option.
